content: The nuclear meltdown at Chernobyl in 1986 resulted in the deaths of numerous humans and animals due to cancer. Additionally, it caused genetic mutations in a significant number of both animals and humans. The area surrounding the Chernobyl plant has been abandoned by humans because of the high levels of radiation released during the meltdown. However, twenty years after the disaster, wildlife has returned to the region. Bibliography: Warming, E. (1909). Oecology of Plants an introduction to the study of plant-communities. Clarendon Press, Oxford. Haeckel, E. (1866). General Morphology of Organisms; General Outlines of the Science of Organic Forms based on Mechanical Principles through the Theory of Descent as reformed by Charles Darwin. Berlin.
